accepted.s: The National Human Rights Commission was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 on
accepted.x: The NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Ordinance preceding the Act was promulgated on 28 September 1993.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the Ordinance from the date of establishment.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 was preceded by an Ordinance promulgated on
accepted.x: The first legal step was the Ordinance of 28 September 1993, followed by the establishment of the NHRC on 12 October 1993.
accepted.tq: Use the close-date trap by separating the Ordinance date from the Commission’s establishment date.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Human Rights Commission conforms to the
accepted.x: The NHRC conforms to the Paris Principles, adopted in Paris in October 1991.
accepted.tq: Test the exact international standard associated with a national human-rights institution.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Paris Principles:
1. They were adopted in Paris in October 1991.
2. They were endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly on 20 December 1993.
3. They exclusively concern the protection of linguistic minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Paris Principles concern national human-rights institutions generally, not exclusively linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that narrows a broad institutional principle into an exclusive category.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Following the 2019 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act, the number of human-rights-expert members in the NHRC became
o: Three, with at least one woman
Three, with at least two women
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment increased the number of human-rights-expert members from two to three and required that at least one of them be a woman.
accepted.tq: Compare the pre-amendment and post-amendment composition figures.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment added the Chairperson of the NCBC, the Chairperson of the NCPCR and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as deemed members. The other listed chairpersons were already included.
accepted.tq: Identify the newly added body rather than a pre-existing deemed member.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a deemed member of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Linguistic Minorities
Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
accepted.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is not listed as a deemed member of the NHRC. The chairpersons of NCW, NCM and NCBC are deemed members.
accepted.tq: Find the body that is absent from the statutory list of deemed members.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the 2019 amendment, the term of office of the Chairperson and members of the NHRC is
o: Six years or until attaining 70 years, whichever is earlier
Five years or until attaining 65 years, whichever is earlier
Three years or until attaining 70 years, whichever is earlier, with reappointment allowed
Three years without any possibility of reappointment
accepted.x: The amended framework provides a term of three years or until the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier, and permits reappointment.
accepted.tq: Read both components of a tenure provision instead of selecting the duration alone.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the Paris Principles
B. Promulgation of the Ordinance preceding the PHRA
C. Establishment of the NHRC
D. Endorsement of the Paris Principles by the UN General Assembly
accepted.x: The Paris Principles were adopted in October 1991, the Ordinance was promulgated on 28 September 1993, the NHRC was established on 12 October 1993, and UNGA endorsement followed on 20 December 1993.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events before arranging the close 1993 dates.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a power exercised by the NHRC while conducting an inquiry?
o: Power to amend the law under which the inquiry is conducted
Power to impose a binding monetary penalty on the Union Government
Powers of a civil court for summoning witnesses and calling for documents
Power to punish every witness for contempt without judicial process
accepted.x: During inquiries, the NHRC has the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, calling for documents and receiving evidence on affidavit. It cannot itself amend legislation or impose a binding monetary penalty on the government.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority has the procedural power rather than the final coercive power.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations of the NHRC:
1. They are binding on the government.
2. The government is required to respond to them.
3. The Commission cannot compel implementation of its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NHRC recommendations are not binding. However, the government must respond, and the Commission cannot compel their implementation.
accepted.tq: Separate the duty to respond from the power to compel implementation.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A complaint alleging a human-rights violation committed eighteen months ago is ordinarily outside the jurisdiction of the NHRC because the Commission
o: cannot inquire into an incident after one year from its occurrence
has jurisdiction only over incidents occurring outside India
can inquire only after a criminal conviction
can inquire only into incidents committed by private persons
accepted.x: The NHRC cannot inquire into a complaint after one year from the date of the alleged violation.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory time-bar rule to a factual situation.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In relation to alleged human-rights violations by members of the armed forces, the NHRC may primarily
o: transfer the case to a State Human Rights Commission
issue a binding order to the commanding officer
seek a report from the Central Government
accepted.x: The NHRC’s role concerning the armed forces is limited; it may seek a report from the Central Government and act within the statutory framework.
accepted.tq: Use the limited-power trap where a reporting power is mistaken for direct enforcement.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment

accepted.s: A State Human Rights Commission may inquire into violations relating to
o: any subject, including matters exclusively under the Union List
State List and Concurrent List subjects
accepted.x: The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to human-rights violations relating to subjects in the State List and the Concurrent List.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State Commission’s subject jurisdiction from that of the national body.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment

accepted.s: A State Human Rights Commission shall not ordinarily take up a matter that is already before
o: the NHRC or another statutory commission
accepted.x: An SHRC does not take up a case already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
accepted.tq: Identify the jurisdictional bar created by parallel proceedings before another statutory commission.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. National Commission for Minorities — Statutory body
2. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Constitutional office
3. NITI Aayog — Body created by a constitutional provision
accepted.x: The NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992, and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is a constitutional office under Article 350B. NITI Aayog was created by a Cabinet resolution, not by the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional, statutory and executive bases of creation.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs statutory status of bodies (NCM, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Commission for Minorities derives its statutory status from the
accepted.x: The NCM is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
accepted.tq: Use the body–enabling law association rather than the date of an executive resolution.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs statutory status of bodies (NCM, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
(a) National Development Council — Executive resolution
(b) Planning Commission — Executive resolution
(c) Zonal Councils — States Reorganisation Act, 1956
(d) National Commission for Backward Classes — Executive resolution
o: National Commission for Backward Classes — Executive resolution
accepted.x: The NCB​​C is a constitutional body under Article 338B, not a body created by executive resolution. The NDC and Planning Commission were created through executive resolutions, while Zonal Councils derive from the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly assigned legal basis among closely related institutions.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs statutory status of bodies (NCM, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Linguistic minorities in India are primarily dealt with by the
o: National Commission for Women under the NCW Act
Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B
National Human Rights Commission under the PHRA
National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act
accepted.x: Linguistic minorities are not notified under the NCM Act; their constitutional protection is associated with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between religious minorities under the NCM framework and linguistic minorities under Article 350B.
accepted.sec: Constitutional vs statutory status of bodies (NCM, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of communities notified as minorities by the Government of India is
accepted.x: Six communities are notified: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. The notification concerning these communities was issued on 27 January 2014.
accepted.tq: Count the notified communities and avoid omitting the later-listed Jain community.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following communities is included among the minorities notified by the Government of India?
o: Linguistic minorities as a general category
accepted.x: Jains are among the six notified minority communities, along with Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis. Linguistic minorities are not notified under the NCM Act as a general category.
accepted.tq: Test membership in a notified list against constitutionally protected but separately classified groups.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With regard to the National Commission for Minorities, which of the following statements is correct?
1. It is appointed by the Central Government.
2. Its members are appointed by the President.
3. Five members including the Chairperson belong to minority communities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The NCM is appointed by the Central Government, not by the President. Five of its seven members, including the Chairperson, are from minority communities.
accepted.tq: Separate the appointing authority from the composition requirement.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Commission for Women comprises a Chairperson,
o: five members including at least one member from the SC and one from the ST, and a Member-Secretary
five members from minority communities and a Vice-Chairperson
three members including one woman and a Member-Secretary
seven members and a Chief Commissioner
accepted.x: The NCW consists of a Chairperson, five members, at least one of whom is from the SC and at least one from the ST, and a Member-Secretary.
accepted.tq: Reconstruct the statutory composition from its distinctive inclusion requirements.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The tenure of the National Commission for Women is
accepted.x: The Chairperson and members of the NCW have a tenure of three years. They may be removed by the Central Government in accordance with the applicable provisions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three-year tenure of the NCW from the earlier five-year NHRC tenure.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Commission for Women is appointed and its members are nominated by the
accepted.x: The NCW is constituted through nomination by the Central Government, unlike the NHRC, whose members are appointed by the President.
accepted.tq: Compare the appointing authority of different national commissions.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NCPCR is a statutory body established under the
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
accepted.x: The NCPCR was established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, although it monitors the implementation of several other child-related laws.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its constituting statute rather than a law it monitors.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s:
Which of the following enactments are monitored by the NCPCR?
1. Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
2. Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
3. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
4. National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The NCPCR monitors the RTE Act, 2009, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015. The National Commission for Minorities Act is not part of this child-rights monitoring mandate.
accepted.tq: Remove the unrelated statute from a cluster of child-rights laws.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s: The NCPCR’s mandate includes examining whether laws and policies are in conformity with the
o: Paris Agreement and the Constitution alone
Convention against Torture and the Geneva Conventions
Constitution of India and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights alone
accepted.x: The NCPCR keeps laws and policies in line with the Constitution and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. India acceded to the UNCRC in 1992.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired domestic and international foundations of the child-rights mandate.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s: India acceded to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in
accepted.x: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989, and India acceded to it in 1992.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of adoption of an international convention from India’s accession year.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s: Which one of the following bodies, along with State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights, monitors the implementation of the POCSO Act?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
accepted.x: The NCPCR and the State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights monitor the implementation of the POCSO Act, 2012.
accepted.tq: Identify the specialised child-rights institutions rather than a general statutory body.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s: The Right to Education provision monitored by the NCPCR concerning 25 per cent free seats is found in Section
accepted.x: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 concerns the 25 per cent reservation of seats for children in specified private unaided schools.
accepted.tq: Match the precise statutory section with the policy obligation it contains.
accepted.sec: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about international human-rights documents:
1. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in 1948.
2. The ICCPR and ICESCR were adopted in 1966.
3. CEDAW was adopted in 1979.
4. The Convention against Torture was adopted in 1984.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the UDHR dates to 1948, the ICCPR and ICESCR to 1966, CEDAW to 1979 and the Convention against Torture to 1984.
accepted.tq: Arrange a compact list of dates without allowing one familiar year to distort the others.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December in commemoration of the adoption of the
o: Convention on the Rights of the Child
International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
accepted.x: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December to commemorate the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.
accepted.tq: Link the commemorative date to the correct international instrument.
accepted.sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]
